items.title: Architecture diff between revisions
items.blurb: asbuilt diff main..HEAD names how the architecture changed between two commits (modules added, relations moved), and the action can post it on a pull request.

acceptance.criterion: asbuilt diff <a>..<b> names each element and relation added, removed, or changed between the two revisions
Two revisions with the same architecture report no change
--format json names the changes in the shape check --format json does
--format markdown writes the comment the action posts on a pull request

items.title: Architecture rules
items.blurb: Rules you declare (no cycles, which layers may depend on which), checked like drift and reported the same way.

acceptance.criterion: asbuilt conform exits 1 and names each relation that breaks a rule declared in asbuilt.toml
A model that keeps every declared rule passes with exit 0
asbuilt check still reports drift alone: a broken rule does not fail it

items.title: Edges that list only what they draw
items.blurb: An edge's popover lists the relations that edge draws, not every relation between its endpoints, so a filtered view stays filtered.

acceptance.criterion: In a view that draws only some of the relations between two elements, an edge's popover lists only the ones it draws
In a view that draws every relation between them, the popover lists them all

items.title: Site styles generated in Rust
items.blurb: The landing page's utility classes become CSS through encre-css, a Rust crate, in a host test that commits the stylesheet, so the site's build downloads no Tailwind binary.

acceptance.criterion: The committed stylesheet is the one encre-css generates from the components, so a class added or removed without regenerating fails the site's tests
Every class the components name has a rule, in the generated utilities or in the page's own CSS
The page links only plain stylesheets from the tree, so Trunk runs no CSS tool

items.title: A second language: Python
items.blurb: A Python front-end, dogfooded on a FastAPI code base: packages to containers, modules to components, imports to relations, and the docs pages in Python's own words.

acceptance.criterion: A Python project surveys to a model: packages to containers, modules to components, and imports to relations
The docs pages call a Python model's elements packages and modules

items.title: Installing without cargo
items.blurb: An install script that checks the release's attestation, and a Homebrew tap, for teams without a Rust toolchain.

acceptance.criterion: The install script refuses an archive whose attestation does not verify, and installs nothing
The Homebrew formula installs the release archive for each macOS and Linux target

items.title: Coupling metrics
items.blurb: Coupling metrics per crate and module on their pages.

acceptance.criterion: Each crate's and module's page shows its afferent and efferent coupling and its instability
Coupling is counted from the model's relations between elements, not from item references

items.title: Dependencies as externals
items.blurb: Opt-in externals from Cargo.toml, and crate-to-crate summaries on each container page.

acceptance.criterion: With the opt-in, each dependency in Cargo.toml is an external, with a relation from the crate that declares it
Without the opt-in, the model is unchanged
Each container page summarizes its crate-to-crate relations

items.blurb: Know which modules and relations a feature or platform turns on.

items.blurb: An option to embed LikeC4's own web component: element details, a relationship browser, search.
